subject: dsa
title: Container With Most Water
summary: Each bar is a wall. Start wide and always move the shorter wall inward — that's the only move that can ever increase the trapped area.
problem: Each value is a wall height. Find the two walls that, with the x-axis, hold the most water.

steps.caption: Each bar is a wall. Pick two walls holding the most water. Area = width between them x the shorter wall.
Start wide: L=0, R=5. Area = 5 x min(1, 7) = 5. The left wall is shorter, so move L inward.
L=1, R=5. Area = 4 x min(8, 7) = 28 — our best yet! Now the right wall is shorter, so move R inward.
L=1, R=4. Area = 3 x min(8, 5) = 15. Smaller than 28. Right wall is shorter — move R.
L=1, R=3. Area = 2 x min(8, 2) = 4. Right wall shorter — move R.
L=1, R=2. Area = 1 x min(8, 6) = 6. The pointers are about to meet.
Done. The most water was 28, held by the walls at index 1 (height 8) and index 5 (height 7).
